mainTopic: כוונה in blowing שופר, and who can be מוציא others in שופר and ברכות.
overview: This amud opens with the end of רבי זירא's instruction to the blower: 'Have כוונה and blow for me.' The גמרא learns from this that the blower must have כוונה for the listener. It defends this view against a משנה by saying the משנה speaks of a שליח ציבור, who has everyone in mind. It then shows the question is a dispute between תנאים, and that רבי זירא follows רבי יוסי. A new משנה teaches that משה's raised hands and the copper snake worked only when Israel turned their hearts to ה׳. It then rules that a חרש, שוטה, or קטן cannot blow for others, because only someone who is obligated can be מוציא others. The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing who is obligated in שופר and who can blow for whom, and explains why כהנים had to be mentioned. רב הונא and רב נחמן argue whether a half-slave is יוצא even for himself, and a ברייתא supports רב נחמן that he is not. Finally, אהבה בריה דרבי זירא teaches that most ברכות can be said for others even after one is יוצא, except the ברכות on bread and wine, and רבא begins a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי זירא tells the blower to have intent for him
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells his attendant to have כוונה and blow for him. The גמרא concludes that he holds the blower needs כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Have intent and blow the שופר for me.' So it seems he holds that the one who blows needs intent.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רבי זירא's instruction to the person blowing שופר for him. The גמרא then draws a rule from it: the מַשְׁמִיעַ must have כוונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא did not settle for simply hearing the שופר. He specifically asked the blower to have him in mind. From this the גמרא learns that, in his view, the listener is not יוצא unless the blower intends to make him יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who makes others hear (the blower)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the target of everything that follows next. Each challenge tests whether 'the blower needs כוונה' can hold up.

phrases.english: Have intent and blow for me.
phrases.notes: רבי זירא speaking to his attendant (continued earlier).

phrases.english: Apparently he holds:
The one who blows needs intent.
phrases.notes: This means intent to make the listener יוצא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a legal rule from רבי זירא's instruction earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי זירא, the מַשְׁמִיעַ must have כוונה to make the listener יוצא.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about someone passing behind a synagogue
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that a passerby who hears the שופר is יוצא if he had כוונה. But the blower never had this passerby in mind!
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: If someone was walking behind a בית הכנסת, or his house was next to the בית הכנסת, and he heard the sound of the שופר or of the מגילה, then if he focused his heart he is יוצא, and if not he is not יוצא. But even if he focused his heart, what good is that? The other one (the blower) did not have him in mind!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא using a משנה. In that משנה, only the listener's כוונה is mentioned, and he is יוצא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blower inside the בית הכנסת does not even know the passerby exists, so he cannot have him in mind. If the blower needed כוונה for the listener, the passerby should never be יוצא. Yet the משנה says he is יוצא, which seems to contradict רבי זירא.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one (here this means הַהוּא, not 'how')

steps.confusionAlert: Here הֵיאַךְ does NOT mean 'how.' In this Aramaic it means 'that other person,' referring to the blower. Read it as: 'The other one did not have him in mind!'

phrases.english: They challenged:
If one was passing behind a synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בֵּיתוֹ סָמוּךְ לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת,
phrases.english: or his house was next to the synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁמַע קוֹל שׁוֹפָר אוֹ קוֹל מְגִילָּה,
phrases.english: and he heard the sound of the shofar or the sound of the Megillah,
if he focused his heart, he has fulfilled his obligation,
and if not, he has not fulfilled it.
But if he focused his heart, what good is that?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is now asking this according to רבי זירא.

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ לָא קָא מִיכַּוֵּין אַדַּעְתָּא דִּידֵיהּ!
phrases.english: The other one (the blower) did not have him in mind!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule just derived from רבי זירא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's rule that the מַשְׁמִיעַ needs כוונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets a random passerby be יוצא through his own כוונה alone. The blower could not have intended to include him, so the blower's כוונה seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The משנה is about a community prayer leader who has everyone in mind
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is speaking about a שליח ציבור, whose כוונה covers everyone who hears.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a community prayer leader, whose intent is for the whole world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי זירא. It explains that the blower in the משנה is a שליח ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שליח ציבור blows with the intent to make every listener יוצא, even people he does not know about. So the passerby really is covered by the blower's כוונה. The משנה therefore does not contradict רבי זירא.

keyTerms.meaning: Community prayer leader / representative of the congregation

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with a community prayer leader,
whose intent is on everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בִּשְׁלִיחַ צִיבּוּר עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the blower had no intent for the passerby.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שליח ציבור intends to include anyone who hears, so the blower's כוונה does exist.

steps.title: Second challenge: a ברייתא treats the blower like the listener
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא requires both the listener and the blower to have כוונה. It compares them, which implies the blower only needs כוונה for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If the listener had intent but the blower did not, or the blower had intent but the listener did not, he is not יוצא, until both the listener and the blower have intent. The ברייתא teaches the blower similar to the listener. Just as the listener hears for himself, so too the blower blows for himself. And it teaches that without this he is not יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רבי זירא from a ברייתא. It does this by comparing the two people the ברייתא mentions side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the blower in parallel to the listener. The listener's כוונה is clearly for himself, so the blower's כוונה should also be just for himself, meaning to do the מצוה. That suggests the blower does not need כוונה for the listener, which contradicts רבי זירא.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא itself says the blower needs כוונה, which sounds like it supports רבי זירא. The challenge comes from the comparison: the כוונה it requires is for himself, not for the listener.
steps.whatToRemember: The question is not WHETHER the blower needs כוונה, but WHAT KIND. רבי זירא says he needs כוונה for the listener. The ברייתא, by comparing him to the listener, implies he needs only כוונה for himself.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If the listener had intent but the blower did not,
or the blower had intent but the listener did not,
he has not fulfilled his obligation,
until both the listener and the blower have intent.
It teaches the blower parallel to the listener.
Just as the listener hears for himself,
so too the blower blows for himself,
and it teaches that (without this) he is not yotzei.
phrases.notes: This implies that intent for himself is enough, against רבי זירא.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 3 resolved the first challenge, this opens a second attack on רבי זירא's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's rule that the מַשְׁמִיעַ needs כוונה for the listener
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא compares the blower to the listener. Since the listener's כוונה is for himself, the blower's required כוונה should also be only for himself, so כוונה for the listener is not needed.

steps.title: The question is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the role of the blower's כוונה is debated by תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא where the תנא קמא says the blower may simply blow in his normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: The listener hears for himself, and the blower blows in his normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from step 4. It says the sources conflict because תנאים disagree, and it starts quoting the ברייתא that shows the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא does not need to fit every source. According to the first opinion here, only the listener needs כוונה, and the blower can blow 'in his normal way' with no special intent for the listener. This sets up the contrasting view of רבי יוסי in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
The one who makes others hear, meaning the blower
In his normal way, without special intent for the listener

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim,
phrases.notes: The answer to the קשיא: רבי זירא follows one side of a dispute.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a Baraita:
The listener hears for himself,
phrases.notes: The listener's own כוונה is what counts.

phrases.english: and the blower blows in his normal way.
phrases.notes: He does not need intent to fulfill the listener's obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by turning the conflict into a dispute between תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מחלוקת תנאים: the opposing source reflects a different תנא's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All sources agree that the blower only needs כוונה for himself, so רבי זירא is contradicted.
steps.terutzMaskana: תנאים disagree on this point, so רבי זירא can follow one side.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: an individual blower needs intent for the listener
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי limits the first opinion to a שליח ציבור. With a private individual, the listener is יוצא only if both the listener and the blower have כוונה, which matches רבי זירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: When is this said? With a community representative. But with an individual, he is not יוצא until both the listener and the blower have intent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives the other side of the dispute. רבי זירא's view from step 1 matches רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a שליח ציבור, his general כוונה covers everyone, which matches the answer in step 3. For a private person blowing for someone, the blower must have that specific listener in mind. This is exactly why רבי זירא told his attendant to blow with כוונה for him.

keyTerms.meaning: When is this statement said? (a formula that limits a rule)

steps.whatToRemember: Whether the blower needs כוונה for the listener is a dispute between תנאים. According to רבי יוסי, whom רבי זירא follows, a שליח ציבור's general כוונה covers everyone, but a private blower must have the specific listener in mind.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
When is this said? With a community representative,
but with an individual, he is not יוצא,
until both the listener and the blower have intent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 5 by giving the opinion that supports רבי זירא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי זירא follows רבי יוסי: a private blower must have כוונה for the listener, while a שליח ציבור's general כוונה covers everyone.

steps.title: משה's raised hands and the war with עמלק
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks whether משה's hands really won or lost the war. It answers that Israel won when they looked upward and gave their hearts to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: 'And when משה raised his hand, Israel prevailed.' Did משה's hands make or break the war? Rather, as long as Israel looked upward and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven, they prevailed. If not, they fell.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains a פסוק about משה's hands to teach that the victory came from Israel's hearts turning to ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'Did משה's hands make war?' is rhetorical. It shows that the hands were not the real cause. Raised hands led the people to look up and connect to ה׳, and that inner focus brought victory. This fits the theme of כוונה, the inner direction of the heart.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really so that...? (introduces a rhetorical question)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new halachic rule about שופר. It is an aggadic teaching that the משנה brings here because the topic connects to כוונה.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
"And it was, when Moshe raised his hand,
Israel prevailed, etc."
Did the hands of Moshe
make war or break war?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: the hands themselves did nothing.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to tell you:
as long as Israel
looked upward
and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven,
they prevailed,
and if not, they fell.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי יָדָיו שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה עוֹשׂוֹת מִלְחָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It connects in theme to the discussion of כוונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה's hands did not win the war. Israel's turning their hearts to ה׳ is what brought victory.

steps.title: The copper snake healed through looking up to ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a parallel example. The snake on the pole did not heal or kill. The people were healed when they turned their hearts to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly you say: 'Make for yourself a fiery serpent and set it on a pole, and anyone bitten who sees it will live.' Does a snake kill or give life? Rather, when Israel looked upward and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven, they were healed. If not, they wasted away.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second, matching example to strengthen the same lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The structure is the same as with משה's hands: a פסוק, a rhetorical question, and the answer 'Rather...'. The physical object was only a reminder to look upward. The real healing came from the people's connection to ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Wasting away or rotting (from the bites)

phrases.english: Similarly, you say:
"Make for yourself a fiery serpent
and set it upon a pole,
and anyone who was bitten
and sees it will live."

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי נָחָשׁ מֵמִית, אוֹ נָחָשׁ מְחַיֶּה?
phrases.english: Does a snake kill, or does a snake give life?
Rather, when Israel
looked upward
and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven,
they were healed,
and if not, they wasted away.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּיּוֹצֵא בַּדָּבָר אַתָּה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel example that reinforces the lesson of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The snake did not heal. The people's turning to ה׳ is what healed them.

steps.title: Only someone who is obligated can fulfill the מצוה for others
steps.stepSummary: The משנה returns to halacha. A חרש, שוטה, or קטן cannot be מוציא the רבים, because anyone not obligated in a מצוה cannot fulfill it for others.
steps.simpleTranslation: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor cannot fulfill the obligation for the many. This is the rule: anyone who is not obligated in the matter cannot fulfill the obligation for the many.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes back to the laws of שופר. It rules on who may blow on behalf of others and gives a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חרש, שוטה, and קטן are not obligated in מצוות. The זה הכלל expands the list into a principle: to be מוציא others, you must be obligated yourself. This rule applies widely, not only to שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor
Fulfill the obligation on behalf of others

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a basic principle across halacha for being מוציא others, for example with קידוש and מגילה.
steps.whatToRemember: Only someone who is obligated in a מצוה can fulfill it on behalf of others.

phrases.english: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן.
phrases.english: cannot fulfill the obligation for the many.
This is the general rule:
anyone who is not obligated in the matter

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן.
phrases.english: cannot fulfill the obligation for the many.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחוּיָּיב בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the aggadic teaching to the halacha of who may blow שופר for others.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone not obligated in a מצוה, such as a חרש, שוטה, or קטן, cannot be מוציא others.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists everyone obligated in שופר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא saying that everyone is obligated in תקיעת שופר. This includes כהנים, לוים, ישראלים, גרים, freed slaves, a טומטום, an אנדרוגינוס, and someone who is חציו עבד וחציו בן חורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: Everyone is obligated in blowing the שופר. This includes כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים; גרים and freed slaves; a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס; and one who is half slave and half free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא gives a list of the people who are obligated to hear the שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list moves from the most obvious cases (כהנים, לוים, ישראלים) to cases where you might have doubted the obligation. A טומטום has no visible sign of being male or female. An אנדרוגינוס has signs of both. A person who is חציו עבד וחציו בן חורין is partly a slave and partly free. The ברייתא includes all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
A person whose gender cannot be seen, so it is uncertain
A person with both male and female features
A person who is half slave and half free

steps.confusionAlert: The word "obligated" here means obligated to HEAR the שופר. Each person does not have to blow it himself.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Rabbis taught:
Everyone is obligated in blowing the shofar.
Kohanim, Levites, and Israelites;
converts and freed slaves;
and a tumtum and an androginos;
one who is half slave
and half free.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בִּתְקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה said a חרש, שוטה, or קטן cannot blow for others. The גמרא now brings a ברייתא that spells out who IS obligated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All Jews are obligated in תקיעת שופר, including people of uncertain or mixed status.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list sets up the next rule. Being obligated in general does not always mean you can blow for every other person.

steps.title: Who can blow for whom: טומטום, אנדרוגינוס, and half-slave
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. A טומטום cannot blow for anyone. An אנדרוגינוס can blow for another אנדרוגינוס, but not for anyone else. A half-slave cannot blow for anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טומטום cannot exempt his own kind, nor someone not of his kind. An אנדרוגינוס can exempt his own kind, but not someone not of his kind. One who is half slave and half free cannot exempt his own kind, nor someone not of his kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains which of these doubtful-status people can blow the שופר on behalf of others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This applies the rule from step 9: someone who is not fully obligated cannot blow for someone who is. A טומטום might be a woman, and women are exempt from שופר. So he cannot blow for anyone, not even another טומטום, since the blower might be female and the listener male. Two אנדרוגינוס have the exact same status, so one can blow for the other. A half-slave cannot blow for anyone, because his slave half cannot exempt the free half of the listener.

keyTerms.meaning: Fulfills the מצוה on someone else's behalf
His own kind (someone with the same status)
Someone not of his kind (a regular man or woman)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the טומטום with the אנדרוגינוס. The טומטום's status is an uncertainty that may differ from person to person. The אנדרוגינוס is always treated the same way, so two of them always match.
steps.whatToRemember: Even if you are obligated, you can only be מוציא someone whose obligation is not greater than your own.

phrases.aramaic: טוּמְטוּם — אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא לֹא אֶת מִינוֹ,
phrases.english: A tumtum cannot exempt his own kind,
nor someone who is not of his kind.
An androginos can exempt his own kind,
but not someone who is not of his kind.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין —
phrases.english: One who is half slave and half free
cannot exempt his own kind,
nor someone who is not of his kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְטוּם — אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא לֹא אֶת מִינוֹ, וְלֹא אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא. It moves from who is obligated to who can blow for others.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טומטום and a half-slave cannot blow for anyone. An אנדרוגינוס can blow only for another אנדרוגינוס.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the step 9 principle at work. Being obligated is not enough. The blower's obligation must fully cover the listener's obligation.

steps.title: Why list כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים? That is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of the ברייתא and asks why it needed to say that כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים are obligated. If they are not obligated, who would be?
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Everyone is obligated in blowing the שופר, כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים. That is obvious! If these are not obligated, who is obligated?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first line of the ברייתא and challenges it as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא never wastes words. Saying that ordinary Jews are obligated seems pointless, since they are the most basic people a מצוה applies to. So the גמרא wants to know what this line adds.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said" (quotes a line from the earlier source)
"It is obvious!" (a challenge that something is unnecessary)

phrases.english: The Master said:
Everyone is obligated in blowing the shofar,
Kohanim, Levites, and Israelites.
That is obvious!
If these are not obligated,
who is obligated?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בִּתְקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר, כֹּהֲנִים לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים. פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opening words of the ברייתא from step 10 and questions why they are needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's mention of כהנים, לוים, and ישראלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These are the most basic people obligated in any מצוה, so listing them seems to add nothing.

steps.title: כהנים needed mention because they blow all year in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא needed to mention כהנים. Since כהנים blow חצוצרות all year over the קרבנות, one might think the 'one-day' שופר obligation of ראש השנה is not meant for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to mention כהנים. You might have thought: since it is written 'It shall be a day of blowing for you,' only someone whose blowing is limited to one day is obligated. כהנים, however, blow all year long, as it is written, 'And you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt-offerings.' So you might say they are not obligated. The ברייתא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. It explains the mistake you might have made without the ברייתא's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "יום תרועה יהיה לכם" describes a single special day of blowing. One could have reasoned that this is aimed at people for whom blowing happens only on that one day. כהנים already blow חצוצרות all year, so you might think they are exempt. The ברייתא lists כהנים to tell us they are obligated like everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was necessary for him" (to say this)
"It could enter your mind to say" (introduces a mistaken assumption)
Trumpets blown by כהנים in the מקדש
"It teaches us" (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: Only כהנים needed this line. לוים and ישראלים are listed just to complete the phrase, since only כהנים blow the חצוצרות.
steps.whatToRemember: This first answer is rejected in the very next step, so do not treat it as the גמרא's final reason. Step 15 gives the answer that stands.

phrases.english: It was necessary for him to mention Kohanim,
since it could enter your mind to say:
Since it is written,
"It shall be a day of blowing for you,"

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּלֵיתֵיהּ אֶלָּא בִּתְקִיעָה דְּחַד יוֹמָא —
phrases.english: someone who is involved only in blowing on one day
is the one who is obligated;
but these Kohanim,
since they are involved in blowing all year long,
as it is written:
"And you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt-offerings,"
I might say they are not obligated.
So it teaches us that they are.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֲנִים אִצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 12 by showing that the line about כהנים is not obvious after all.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the line is needed by naming a reasonable mistake (צריכותא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since כהנים blow חצוצרות all year, the one-day מצוה of יום תרועה might not apply to them.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to this answer, the ברייתא names כהנים to rule out an exemption based on their year-round חצוצרות blowing. Step 14 rejects this reason.

steps.title: Trumpets and שופר are not the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer from Step 13. Blowing חצוצרות all year has nothing to do with blowing a שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they comparable? There it is trumpets, and here it is a שופר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer it just gave about כהנים. Trumpets and a שופר are different instruments, so the comparison does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said that כהנים might be exempt because they already blow חצוצרות all year. The גמרא answers that no one would confuse a חצוצרה with a שופר. So that cannot be why the ברייתא needed to mention כהנים, and the question from Step 12 needs a new answer, which Step 15 gives.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable? (a sign that a comparison is being rejected)
Trumpets, blown by כהנים in the מקדש

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
There it is trumpets, and here it is a shofar!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם חֲצוֹצְרוֹת וְהָכָא שׁוֹפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the full answer from Step 13 about why כהנים had to be mentioned
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison is flawed. חצוצרות and שופר are different instruments, so blowing one would not make someone think they are exempt from the other.

steps.title: The real reason: כהנים are not bound by the laws of יובל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא had to mention כהנים because they are not bound by the land laws of יובל. Since יובל and ראש השנה are linked in שופר and ברכות, one might think כהנים are also exempt from ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was necessary. You might have thought this: since we learned that יובל is like ראש השנה for the תקיעות and the ברכות, whoever is part of the מצוה of יובל is part of the מצוה of ראש השנה. And these כהנים are not part of the מצוה of יובל, as we learned: כהנים and לוים sell forever and redeem forever. So I might say they are not obligated in the מצוה of ראש השנה. The ברייתא teaches us that they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the question of Step 12. It explains why someone might have thought כהנים are exempt from שופר on ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה links the שופר of יובל (blown on יום כיפור) to the שופר of ראש השנה. So one might reason that only people who are part of יובל are part of ראש השנה. כהנים and לוים are not bound by the usual יובל time limits on sales: they may sell and redeem their property at any time. So the ברייתא tells us that כהנים are still obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it was necessary (a new answer is coming)
It could enter your mind to say (a possible mistaken thought)
The 50th year, when land returns to its original owners
They sell forever and redeem forever. כהנים and לוים are not bound by יובל land rules.

steps.confusionAlert: The שופר of יובל is blown on יום כיפור of the יובל year, not on ראש השנה. The משנה only says the two are similar in their תקיעות and ברכות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the שופר obligation of ראש השנה does not depend on being part of יובל. It applies to everyone, כהנים included.

phrases.english: Rather, it was necessary:
It could enter your mind to say,
since we learned in a משנה:
The Jubilee is the same as Rosh HaShana
for the blowing and for the blessings,
so whoever is included in the מצוה of the Jubilee
is included in the מצוה of Rosh HaShana,
and these priests,
since they are not included in the מצוה of the Jubilee,
as we learned in a משנה:
Priests and Levites sell their fields forever
and redeem them forever,

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: בְּמִצְוָה דְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לֹא לִיחַיְּיבוּ —
phrases.english: I might say that they should not be obligated in the מצוה of Rosh HaShana
so it teaches us that they are.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִצְטְרִיךְ: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in Step 14 with a new one
steps.terutzResolutionType: New הוה אמינא that justifies the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since כהנים are not bound by יובל, and יובל is linked to ראש השנה, כהנים might be exempt from שופר on ראש השנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: כהנים are fully obligated in שופר on ראש השנה. The link between יובל and ראש השנה does not limit who is obligated.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא mentions כהנים because their exemption from יובל land laws might have suggested they are exempt from ראש השנה. They are not.

steps.title: רב הונא: The half-slave can be יוצא for himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's ruling that a half-slave cannot blow for anyone. רב הונא adds that he can still fulfill the מצוה for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who is half slave and half free cannot fulfill the obligation for his own kind or for anyone not of his kind. רב הונא said: but for himself he can fulfill it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the ברייתא from Step 11, the half-slave. רב הונא adds a limit: the ruling is only about blowing for other people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the half-slave cannot blow even for another half-slave like himself. רב הונא understands this as a problem only with blowing for others. His own blowing still counts for his own obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Half slave and half free (for example, one of two owners freed him)
He fulfills the obligation for himself

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין —
phrases.english: One who is half slave and half free
cannot fulfill the obligation for his own kind
nor for one who is not his kind.
Rav Huna said:
But for himself he does fulfill it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the half-slave clause of the ברייתא from Step 11 to add רב הונא's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A half-slave cannot blow for others, but according to רב הונא he fulfills the מצוה for himself.

steps.title: רב נחמן: The same problem applies to himself
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רב הונא: if the slave side cannot be מוציא a free side in someone else, it also cannot be מוציא the free side in himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רב הונא: Why can he not do it for others? Because the slave side cannot come and fulfill the obligation of the free side. Then for himself too, his own slave side cannot fulfill the obligation of his own free side.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges רב הונא's ruling. He uses the same reason that stops the half-slave from blowing for others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason a half-slave cannot blow for others is that his slave side is not obligated, so it cannot fulfill a free side's obligation. The same split exists inside his own body. His slave side cannot fulfill the obligation of his own free side either, so רב הונא's distinction falls apart.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Rav Huna:
What is the reason he cannot do it for others?
Because the slave side cannot come
and fulfill the obligation of the free side.
For himself too,
his own slave side cannot come
and fulfill the obligation of his own free side.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא: מַאי שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's ruling in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that the half-slave can be יוצא for himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason he cannot blow for others is the slave side failing to cover a free side. That reason applies equally inside one person, so he should not be יוצא for himself either.

steps.title: רב נחמן: Not even for himself
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the half-slave cannot fulfill the מצוה even for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said: Even for himself he cannot fulfill the obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רב הונא's view, רב נחמן gives his own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows from רב נחמן's challenge. His own slave side cannot fulfill the obligation of his own free side, so his blowing does not count even for himself.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disagrees with רב הונא

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman said:
Even for himself he cannot fulfill the obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אַף לְעַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the challenge of Step 17, replacing רב הונא's view
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A half-slave cannot fulfill the obligation of שופר for himself or for anyone else.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב נחמן said.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: One who is half slave and half free cannot fulfill the obligation even for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב נחמן with a ברייתא that states his ruling word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's ruling is much stronger when a ברייתא, from the earlier תנאים, says the same thing. This settles the matter in favor of רב נחמן over רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports the view)

steps.whatToRemember: The half-slave cannot fulfill the מצוה of שופר for anyone, not even for himself. This is רב נחמן's view, and a ברייתא supports it.

phrases.english: This was also taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין —
phrases.english: One who is half slave and half free
cannot fulfill the obligation even for himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן's ruling in Step 18
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that a half-slave is not יוצא even for himself
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states the same ruling explicitly

steps.title: Most blessings can be said for others even after you already said them, except bread and wine
steps.stepSummary: אהבה בריה דרבי זירא teaches a ברייתא. For most ברכות, a person who already fulfilled his obligation can still be מוציא others. The ברכה on bread and wine is different: he can be מוציא others only if he has not yet fulfilled his own obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: אהבה, the son of רבי זירא, taught: With all the blessings, even if a person already fulfilled his own obligation, he can still fulfill it for others. The exception is the blessing over bread and the blessing over wine. If he has not yet fulfilled his obligation, he can fulfill it for others. But if he already fulfilled it, he cannot fulfill it for others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about being מוציא others with a ברכה. It sets up a general rule and one clear exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most ברכות are obligations of a מצוה. Since all Jews are responsible for each other (ערבות), someone who already did the מצוה still has a share in his friend's obligation, so he can say it for him. The ברכה on bread and wine is different. It is a ברכה of enjoyment (ברכות הנהנין), and it belongs only to the person who is eating or drinking. Someone who already made his own ברכה and is not eating now has no part in it, so he cannot say it for others.

keyTerms.meaning: he fulfills the obligation on behalf of others
blessings said over enjoyment, such as food and drink

steps.confusionAlert: The exception does NOT mean you can never say the ברכה on bread or wine for others. You can, as long as you have not yet fulfilled your own obligation, for example when you are eating together with them. The only limit is after you have already fulfilled your obligation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for a well-known halacha. One who already made קידוש or a מצוה ברכה can repeat it for someone else. But one who is not eating cannot make the המוציא or the wine ברכה for others.

phrases.english: Ahava, son of Rabbi Zeira, taught:
All the blessings, all of them,
even though he already fulfilled his obligation, he can discharge others' obligation.
except for the blessing over bread and the blessing over wine,
where if he has not fulfilled his obligation, he can discharge others,
but if he already fulfilled it, he cannot discharge others.
phrases.notes: A blessing of enjoyment belongs only to the one who is enjoying.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי אַהֲבָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of being מוציא others (from the שופר discussion) and widens it to ברכות in general.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For מצוה ברכות, one can be מוציא others even after fulfilling his own obligation. For the bread and wine ברכות, he can be מוציא others only if he has not yet fulfilled his own.

steps.title: רבא begins to ask a question
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a question. The content of the question comes in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only a setup line. The גמרא is opening רבא's question, and the actual question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בעי signals a real halachic dilemma, not an attack. רבא will build on the rule just taught about who can be מוציא others with a ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: asked or raised a dilemma (a genuine question, not a challenge)

phrases.english: Rava raised a dilemma:
phrases.notes: The question itself continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a question that builds on אהבה's ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not yet stated on this amud. רבא's dilemma about being מוציא others with ברכות follows in the next section.
